title: Installment Payment Plans: One Plan per Policy Term
content:
**Rule.** Under the **Installment Payment Plans**, a customer may hold any number of payment plans, one for each policy term they are responsible for; there is no limit on the number of plans per customer. Only one payment plan is set up per policy term. A renewal term gets its own new plan, on the plan the customer selects for the renewal; the expiring term's plan is closed under its own rules. A plan bills exactly one term, either an Owner Auto Policy term or a Named Non-Owner Policy term, never both.

**What the records must show.** Whether a term already has a plan is read from the system's plan records for that term — the Owner Auto Policy term or the Named Non-Owner Policy term the plan bills — not from the customer's account of it. A term counts as already having a plan while that plan is enrolled, current, past due, paid in full, final-billed or in collections; a closed plan does not count.

| Situation (hypothetical) | Result |
|---|---|
| Customer holds an owner term and a non-owner term | One plan for each term; two plans in all |
| A term already has a current plan and a second plan is asked for the same term | Not set up: only one plan per term |
| The term's earlier plan is closed | The closed plan does not stand in the way |
| An owner term renews | The renewal term is set up on its own new plan; the expiring term's plan closes under its own rules |
